newsitem.title: UK: Battered rhodium could make comeback at $200.
newsitem.headline: Battered rhodium could make comeback at $200.

text.p: Rhodium prices, which have been battered by U.S. speculator selling over the last week, could remain under pressure until the market hits $200 an ounce.

Rhodium is now around $245, close to a January 1996 low and a mid-1980s nadir of around $230 -- a major retracement from dizzy heights of $7,000 reached in 1990 as booming demand from autocatalyst makers burnt off global supplies.
Traders said estimates of the recent selling varied considerably, from as much as 1.25 tonnes (72,000 ounces) down to a more conservative 5,000 ounces.
"There were few buyers around to soak up the selling which saw the the market nosedive last week," a trader said.
The market is destined for $200 before any stability emerges," another trader said.
Others agreed, saying the speculative source, a buyer around two years ago, decided to liquidate in an illiquid market.
The amount of rhodium held is quite considerable, as 72,000 ounces is nearly equivalent to annual Russian supply.

The buying mostly took place in 1994 when prices ranged roughly between $560 and $930 and was largely a speculative venture, regardless of market fundamentals or global demand. "I think the long just got fed up with the whole scenario and decided to sell, though in such a thin market they found few willing buyers," a trader commented. "Noone is taking a position at the moment as they adopt a wait-and-see attitude," another added.
Some traders suggested that producers may enter the market soon to prop up teetering values, a move that may encourge short-covering.

"I believe the bottom of the market is towards $200 where buying is expected to come into play," a trader said. Global stock levels are at high levels, and the autocatalyst industry will continue to be supplied by long term contracts from the two major producers, South Africa and Russia.
According to platinum group refiner Johnson Matthey Plc the inventory overhang will continue to weigh on prices in 1996.

Johnson Matthey said demand in 1995 jumped to 459,000 ounces from 386,000 in 1994, but supply failed to keep pace, rising 10,000 ounces to 436,000. This created a 23,000 ounce deficit. In Europe on Wednesday rhodium, which is also used in the glass and computer industries, ranged between $230 and $260 an ounce on the free-market.
Meanwhile, Johnson Matthey's daily European price was quoted at $280 an ounce.
